Key.Original: Enable the normal-vision acuity pass, a FilmGrain effect at high sharpness and low intensity. The engine has no Sharpen effect, so this is the scriptable candidate; real scene sharpening is the video option Sharpen Filter, which a mod cannot set. No unit. UNSOURCED that FilmGrain sharpness sharpens the scene.
Key.English: Enable the normal-vision acuity pass, a FilmGrain effect at high sharpness and low intensity. The engine has no Sharpen effect, so this is the scriptable candidate; real scene sharpening is the video option Sharpen Filter, which a mod cannot set. No unit. UNSOURCED that FilmGrain sharpness sharpens the scene.

Key.Original: Acuity Pass
Key.English: Acuity Pass

Key.Original: Black-point offset of the normal-vision grade, no unit, range -0.1 to 0.1. Negative deepens the black. Community code uses -0.01 (AsYetUntitled) and -0.35 (Liberation-RX); the exact default -0.02 is UNSOURCED.
Key.English: Black-point offset of the normal-vision grade, no unit, range -0.1 to 0.1. Negative deepens the black. Community code uses -0.01 (AsYetUntitled) and -0.35 (Liberation-RX); the exact default -0.02 is UNSOURCED.

Key.Original: Base Grade Black Point
Key.English: Base Grade Black Point

Key.Original: Display brightness of the normal-vision grade, range 0.7 to 1.3. BIKI Post Process Effects: ColorCorrections brightness, 0 black, 1 unchanged, 2 white.
Key.English: Display brightness of the normal-vision grade, range 0.7 to 1.3. BIKI Post Process Effects: ColorCorrections brightness, 0 black, 1 unchanged, 2 white.

Key.Original: Base Grade Brightness
Key.English: Base Grade Brightness

Key.Original: Display contrast of the normal-vision grade, range 0.8 to 1.6. The ACES tone scale is an S-shaped curve with a mid-grey log-log gamma below 1.55; the engine contrast is linear, so this is a stand-in. The exact default 1.15 is UNSOURCED.
Key.English: Display contrast of the normal-vision grade, range 0.8 to 1.6. The ACES tone scale is an S-shaped curve with a mid-grey log-log gamma below 1.55; the engine contrast is linear, so this is a stand-in. The exact default 1.15 is UNSOURCED.

Key.Original: Base Grade Contrast
Key.English: Base Grade Contrast

Key.Original: Enable the normal-vision base grade (contrast, brightness, black point and colour weights). It applies on normal vision only and never in a sensor mode, and it owns its own ColorCorrections, so it never fights the weather grade. No unit.
Key.English: Enable the normal-vision base grade (contrast, brightness, black point and colour weights). It applies on normal vision only and never in a sensor mode, and it owns its own ColorCorrections, so it never fights the weather grade. No unit.

Key.Original: Base Grade
Key.English: Base Grade

Key.Original: FilmGrain intensity for the acuity pass, range 0 to 0.05. BIKI FilmGrain default 0.005. The engine couples grain and sharpness, so a small amount of grain is unavoidable with the sharpening.
Key.English: FilmGrain intensity for the acuity pass, range 0 to 0.05. BIKI FilmGrain default 0.005. The engine couples grain and sharpness, so a small amount of grain is unavoidable with the sharpening.

Key.Original: Acuity Grain Intensity
Key.English: Acuity Grain Intensity

Key.Original: Desaturation weight of the normal-vision grade, range 0 to 0.5. BIKI ColorCorrections colorize alpha: 0 keeps the original colour, 1 is black and white. The engine can only desaturate; it cannot oversaturate.
Key.English: Desaturation weight of the normal-vision grade, range 0 to 0.5. BIKI ColorCorrections colorize alpha: 0 keeps the original colour, 1 is black and white. The engine can only desaturate; it cannot oversaturate.

Key.Original: Base Grade Saturation
Key.English: Base Grade Saturation

Key.Original: FilmGrain sharpness for the acuity pass, range 1 to 20. BIKI FilmGrain default 1.25. The wiki does not state what it sharpens, so that it sharpens the scene is UNSOURCED; it is a display-aesthetic compromise, not added human acuity.
Key.English: FilmGrain sharpness for the acuity pass, range 1 to 20. BIKI FilmGrain default 1.25. The wiki does not state what it sharpens, so that it sharpens the scene is UNSOURCED; it is a display-aesthetic compromise, not added human acuity.

Key.Original: Acuity Sharpness
Key.English: Acuity Sharpness

Key.Original: Physics colour temperature (issue #100). When on, the white-balance illuminant and the atmospheric desaturation come from the physics colour temperature (sun elevation and cloud cover) and the acuity grain scales with the light level. The correlated colour temperature uses the Kasten and Young 1989 air mass and the CIE 15:2004 daylight locus; the issue's Tanner Helland approximation is superseded by the loci. When off, the white balance uses the engine ambient colour and the shipped image is unchanged.
Key.English: Physics colour temperature (issue #100). When on, the white-balance illuminant and the atmospheric desaturation come from the physics colour temperature (sun elevation and cloud cover) and the acuity grain scales with the light level. The correlated colour temperature uses the Kasten and Young 1989 air mass and the CIE 15:2004 daylight locus; the issue's Tanner Helland approximation is superseded by the loci. When off, the white balance uses the engine ambient colour and the shipped image is unchanged.

Key.Original: Physics Colour Temperature
Key.English: Physics Colour Temperature

Key.Original: Log post-process and human-vision diagnostics to the RPT. Turn this on before reporting a fault.
Key.English: Log post-process and human-vision diagnostics to the RPT. Turn this on before reporting a fault.

Key.Original: Vision Debug Log
Key.English: Vision Debug Log

Key.Original: Show the one-line perception state on screen while the monitor runs. The overlay is a debug surface, so it ships off. No unit.
Key.English: Show the one-line perception state on screen while the monitor runs. The overlay is a debug surface, so it ships off. No unit.

Key.Original: Perception HUD
Key.English: Perception HUD

Key.Original: Minimum seconds between perception samples, range 0.1 to 2.0. The monitor runs in a per-frame handler at 0.5 s, so the effective floor is 0.5 s. Default 0.5. UNSOURCED.
Key.English: Minimum seconds between perception samples, range 0.1 to 2.0. The monitor runs in a per-frame handler at 0.5 s, so the effective floor is 0.5 s. Default 0.5. UNSOURCED.

Key.Original: Perception Interval
Key.English: Perception Interval

Key.Original: Publish and log the reconstructed player view state each tick. The monitor reads state other modules already publish and writes the aee_optics_perception variables; it reads no pixels. Default on. The sample cadence is the perception interval. UNSOURCED that a 0.5 s sample is the right cadence.
Key.English: Publish and log the reconstructed player view state each tick. The monitor reads state other modules already publish and writes the aee_optics_perception variables; it reads no pixels. Default on. The sample cadence is the perception interval. UNSOURCED that a 0.5 s sample is the right cadence.

Key.Original: Perception Monitor
Key.English: Perception Monitor

Key.Original: Enable the scene-aware shadow distance. The distance follows the sampled scene. The classifier values are re-derived from Adaptive Shadows (Workshop 3792830104); no mod content is copied. The classifier is heuristic and its thresholds are UNSOURCED.
Key.English: Enable the scene-aware shadow distance. The distance follows the sampled scene. The classifier values are re-derived from Adaptive Shadows (Workshop 3792830104); no mod content is copied. The classifier is heuristic and its thresholds are UNSOURCED.

Key.Original: Adaptive Shadow Distance
Key.English: Adaptive Shadow Distance

Key.Original: Camera-turn protection in metres, range 0 to 500. The target grows during a fast turn. The default 0 is UNSOURCED.
Key.English: Camera-turn protection in metres, range 0 to 500. The target grows during a fast turn. The default 0 is UNSOURCED.

Key.Original: Shadow Camera Turn Protection
Key.English: Shadow Camera Turn Protection

Key.Original: Far scene influence percentage, range 0 to 100. A higher value lets distant geometry raise the shadow distance. The default 75 is UNSOURCED.
Key.English: Far scene influence percentage, range 0 to 100. A higher value lets distant geometry raise the shadow distance. The default 75 is UNSOURCED.

Key.Original: Shadow Far Scene Influence
Key.English: Shadow Far Scene Influence

Key.Original: Maximum shadow distance in metres, range 25 to 2000. The target is clamped to the object view distance and the engine maximum. The default 500 matches the previous fixed value and is UNSOURCED.
Key.English: Maximum shadow distance in metres, range 25 to 2000. The target is clamped to the object view distance and the engine maximum. The default 500 matches the previous fixed value and is UNSOURCED.

Key.Original: Shadow Maximum Distance
Key.English: Shadow Maximum Distance

Key.Original: Minimum shadow distance in metres, range 0 to 500. The target never goes below this value. The default 50 is UNSOURCED.
Key.English: Minimum shadow distance in metres, range 0 to 500. The target never goes below this value. The default 50 is UNSOURCED.

Key.Original: Shadow Minimum Distance
Key.English: Shadow Minimum Distance

Key.Original: Movement protection in metres per metre per second, range 0 to 10. The target grows with speed. The default 0.6 is UNSOURCED.
Key.English: Movement protection in metres per metre per second, range 0 to 10. The target grows with speed. The default 0.6 is UNSOURCED.

Key.Original: Shadow Movement Protection
Key.English: Shadow Movement Protection

Key.Original: Opening sensitivity percentage, range 3 to 50. A higher value classifies more scenes as openings. The default 12 is UNSOURCED.
Key.English: Opening sensitivity percentage, range 3 to 50. A higher value classifies more scenes as openings. The default 12 is UNSOURCED.

Key.Original: Shadow Opening Sensitivity
Key.English: Shadow Opening Sensitivity

Key.Original: Optics protection in metres, range 0 to 500. The target grows in optics. The default 0 is UNSOURCED.
Key.English: Optics protection in metres, range 0 to 500. The target grows in optics. The default 0 is UNSOURCED.

Key.Original: Shadow Optics Protection
Key.English: Shadow Optics Protection

Key.Original: Number of screen samples used to classify the scene, range 5 to 25. The default 13 is UNSOURCED.
Key.English: Number of screen samples used to classify the scene, range 5 to 25. The default 13 is UNSOURCED.

Key.Original: Shadow Sample Count
Key.English: Shadow Sample Count

Key.Original: Target frame rate for the shadow governor, range 0 to 240. At 0 the governor is off and the ceiling is the effective maximum. The default 0 is UNSOURCED.
Key.English: Target frame rate for the shadow governor, range 0 to 240. At 0 the governor is off and the ceiling is the effective maximum. The default 0 is UNSOURCED.

Key.Original: Shadow Target FPS
Key.English: Shadow Target FPS

Key.Original: Minimum seconds between shadow scene samples, range 0.10 to 2. The default 0.10 is UNSOURCED.
Key.English: Minimum seconds between shadow scene samples, range 0.10 to 2. The default 0.10 is UNSOURCED.

Key.Original: Shadow Update Interval
Key.English: Shadow Update Interval

Key.Original: Drive the engine view distance from the physics visibility state (fog, haze, rain, night sensitivity, acuity). Mostly lowers view distance in weather - a performance gain
Key.English: Drive the engine view distance from the physics visibility state (fog, haze, rain, night sensitivity, acuity). Mostly lowers view distance in weather - a performance gain

Key.Original: Vision-Driven View Distance
Key.English: Vision-Driven View Distance

Key.Original: Degree of chromatic adaptation D of the human-vision model, range 0 to 1. CIECAM02 defines D = F times (1 - (1/3.6) times exp((-LA - 42) / 92)); F is 0.8 for a dim surround, 0.9 average, 1.0 dark. SOURCED: CIE 159:2004. The default 1.0 is a full adaptation.
Key.English: Degree of chromatic adaptation D of the human-vision model, range 0 to 1. CIECAM02 defines D = F times (1 - (1/3.6) times exp((-LA - 42) / 92)); F is 0.8 for a dim surround, 0.9 average, 1.0 dark. SOURCED: CIE 159:2004. The default 1.0 is a full adaptation.

Key.Original: Vision Adaptation Degree
Key.English: Vision Adaptation Degree

Key.Original: Contrast scale on the human-vision tone stage, range 0.5 to 1.5. It scales the display contrast the Naka-Rushton and CIE L* tangent derives. The exact calibration gain is UNSOURCED.
Key.English: Contrast scale on the human-vision tone stage, range 0.5 to 1.5. It scales the display contrast the Naka-Rushton and CIE L* tangent derives. The exact calibration gain is UNSOURCED.

Key.Original: Vision Contrast Scale
Key.English: Vision Contrast Scale

Key.Original: Maximum desaturation of the human-vision model in a scotopic scene, range 0 to 0.5. Default 0, so the default path ships no tint. The engine ambient is green-biased and the operator rejects the tint. Raise it in AEE Experimental to opt in to the experimental mesopic path. The engine can only desaturate. The exact amplitude is UNSOURCED.
Key.English: Maximum desaturation of the human-vision model in a scotopic scene, range 0 to 0.5. Default 0, so the default path ships no tint. The engine ambient is green-biased and the operator rejects the tint. Raise it in AEE Experimental to opt in to the experimental mesopic path. The engine can only desaturate. The exact amplitude is UNSOURCED.

Key.Original: Vision Mesopic Desaturation
Key.English: Vision Mesopic Desaturation

Key.Original: Enable the physical human-vision model for normal vision. It subsumes the aesthetic base grade in place and reads the eye adaptation model. Default on. Disable it to fall back to the aesthetic base grade.
Key.English: Enable the physical human-vision model for normal vision. It subsumes the aesthetic base grade in place and reads the eye adaptation model. Default on. Disable it to fall back to the aesthetic base grade.

Key.Original: Human-Vision Model
Key.English: Human-Vision Model

Key.Original: Strength of the Purkinje shift of the human-vision model, range 0 to 1. Default 0, so the default path ships no tint. The engine ambient is green-biased and the operator rejects the tint. Raise it in AEE Experimental to opt in to the experimental mesopic path. The hue direction is SOURCED to CIE 1951. The tint amplitude is UNSOURCED.
Key.English: Strength of the Purkinje shift of the human-vision model, range 0 to 1. Default 0, so the default path ships no tint. The engine ambient is green-biased and the operator rejects the tint. Raise it in AEE Experimental to opt in to the experimental mesopic path. The hue direction is SOURCED to CIE 1951. The tint amplitude is UNSOURCED.

Key.Original: Vision Purkinje Strength
Key.English: Vision Purkinje Strength

Key.Original: Enable the tone and contrast stage of the human-vision model. It derives the display brightness, contrast and black point from the adapted scene luminance. The form is SOURCED to Naka and Rushton 1966 and CIE 15:2004.
Key.English: Enable the tone and contrast stage of the human-vision model. It derives the display brightness, contrast and black point from the adapted scene luminance. The form is SOURCED to Naka and Rushton 1966 and CIE 15:2004.

Key.Original: Vision Tone Stage
Key.English: Vision Tone Stage

Key.Original: Strength of the human-vision tone stage, range 0 to 1. Default 0.25. The stage is a small bounded rise over the base game's neutral default grade. The anchor clamp keeps the image within a small deviation of that grade. At 0 the stage is the identity. The exact value is UNSOURCED.
Key.English: Strength of the human-vision tone stage, range 0 to 1. Default 0.25. The stage is a small bounded rise over the base game's neutral default grade. The anchor clamp keeps the image within a small deviation of that grade. At 0 the stage is the identity. The exact value is UNSOURCED.

Key.Original: Vision Tone Strength
Key.English: Vision Tone Strength

Key.Original: Enable the partial von Kries white balance of the human-vision model. Default off. The engine ambient under vegetation is green-biased, so full adaptation ships a cast. Turn it on to opt in to the experimental white-balance path. It blends toward the display white D65 (CIE 15:2004) from the scene illuminant. The blend cap is UNSOURCED.
Key.English: Enable the partial von Kries white balance of the human-vision model. Default off. The engine ambient under vegetation is green-biased, so full adaptation ships a cast. Turn it on to opt in to the experimental white-balance path. It blends toward the display white D65 (CIE 15:2004) from the scene illuminant. The blend cap is UNSOURCED.

Key.Original: Vision White Balance
Key.English: Vision White Balance

Key.Original: Intensity scale of the rain-scaled film grain, range 0 to 1. At 0 the grain is not visible. The kernel values are re-derived from Real Lighting and Weather (Workshop 2809399991); no mod content is copied. The exact default 0.5 is UNSOURCED.
Key.English: Intensity scale of the rain-scaled film grain, range 0 to 1. At 0 the grain is not visible. The kernel values are re-derived from Real Lighting and Weather (Workshop 2809399991); no mod content is copied. The exact default 0.5 is UNSOURCED.

Key.Original: Weather Grain Intensity
Key.English: Weather Grain Intensity

Key.Original: Rain level at which the weather film grain engages, range 0 to 1. The grain disengages below half this level, the module hysteresis pattern. The exact default 0.2 is UNSOURCED.
Key.English: Rain level at which the weather film grain engages, range 0 to 1. The grain disengages below half this level, the module hysteresis pattern. The exact default 0.2 is UNSOURCED.

Key.Original: Weather Grain Rain Threshold
Key.English: Weather Grain Rain Threshold
